domain_context: Free-text entries from public clinical trial documentation.

keep.description: Adverse events localized to injection, implant, incision, catheter, or device sites (e.g., pain, hematoma, extravasation, dehiscence).

remove.description: Localized reactions at treatment access points including injection, catheter, or incision sites.
Adverse events related to medical devices, implants, surgical procedures, vaccinations, or access site complications.

keep.description: Inflammatory, infectious, or mucosal damage conditions (e.g., Gastritis, Colitis, Pancreatitis, Ulcers)

remove.description: Localized infections of internal organs excluding skin/respiratory/bloodstream (e.g., GI tract, Genitourinary, Mastitis, Otitis).

candidates.concern: Administration Site Reaction vs Intervention Procedure
Unspecified AE vs Unspecified Study Content

keep.description: New onset or trial-related events affecting the heart, blood vessels, and circulation (e.g., Myocardial Infarction, Arrhythmia, Heart Failure). Excludes baseline cardiovascular conditions.

remove.description: Baseline conditions affecting the heart, blood vessels, and circulation (e.g., CAD, MI, hypertension). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: New onset or trial-related events affecting the brain, spinal cord, nerves, and mental health (e.g., Stroke, Headache, Seizure). Excludes baseline neurological conditions.

remove.description: Baseline conditions affecting the nervous system (e.g., Stroke, Neuralgia, Seizure). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: New onset or trial-related events affecting the digestive system, liver, and biliary tract (e.g., Nausea, Vomiting, Diarrhea, Ulcer). Excludes baseline GI conditions.

remove.description: Baseline conditions affecting the digestive tract and associated organs (e.g., Liver, Pancreas, Cirrhosis). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: Systemic infections involving the blood or resulting in septic shock (e.g., Sepsis, Bacteremia, Candidemia).

remove.description: Baseline conditions caused by pathogenic organisms (e.g., Sepsis, Pneumonia). Excludes new onset infections.

keep.description: New onset or trial-related events affecting the lungs, airways, and breathing (e.g., Respiratory Failure, Dyspnea). Excludes baseline respiratory conditions.

remove.description: Baseline conditions affecting the lungs and airways (e.g., COPD, Asthma). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: New onset events related to blood disorders, coagulation, and blood counts (e.g., Hemorrhage, Thrombocytopenia). Excludes baseline hematologic conditions.

remove.description: Baseline conditions affecting blood and blood-forming organs (e.g., Anemia, Coagulation disorders). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: New onset or trial-related events affecting the skin and underlying tissue (e.g., Rash, Hematoma). Excludes baseline dermatological conditions.

remove.description: Baseline conditions of the skin and subcutaneous tissue (e.g., Rashes, Cysts). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: Alterations in consciousness, cognition, mood, or behavior (e.g., Delirium, Depression, Encephalopathy, Psychomotor).

remove.description: Baseline mental and behavioral health conditions (e.g., Depression, Anxiety). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: Residual cardiovascular events not captured above (e.g., Pericarditis, Chest Pain, Death, Stroke).

remove.description: Baseline conditions affecting the nervous system (e.g., Stroke, Neuralgia, Seizure). Excludes new onset events.

keep.description: Infections affecting the upper or lower respiratory tract and ENT structures (e.g., Pneumonia, Influenza, URI).

remove.description: Baseline conditions caused by pathogenic organisms (e.g., Sepsis, Pneumonia). Excludes new onset infections.

candidates.concern: Safety Outcomes and Adverse Event Incidence

keep.description: Critical life-status events including mortality, late death, and shock states.

remove.description: Single pathological occurrences or procedural needs used as endpoints (e.g., MI, Stroke, Revascularization).
